newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba says four dissidents under arrest.
newsitem.headline: Cuba says four dissidents under arrest.

text.p: The Cuban government said on Thursday that four dissidents were under arrest and were being investigated on suspicion of "counter-revolutionary" activities.

Foreign Ministry spokesman Miguel Alfonso confirmed the arrests in response to questions at a weekly foreign ministry briefing. Diplomatic and dissident sources had said earlier that the four, leading dissidents who run a small opposition group on the Communist-ruled island, were detained by state security officials on Wednesday.
The four detained early Wednesday at their Havana homes were Vladimiro Roca, Martha Beatriz Roque, Felix Bonne and Rene Gomez Manzano.

They run a group called the "Working group of Internal Dissidence" that says it has the support of 14 other small dissident groups in Cuba and is seeking to forge some unity among the small and fragmented opposition. The group has gained increasing prominence abroad in recent months.

Alfonso gave no details of the offences of which the four arested people were supected, other than confirming their names. He said that Cuban law applied to all citizens, whether they were "in favour of, or against, the revolution".

It is extremely unusual for the Cuban authorities to comment on arrests of dissidents or activities by Cuba's small and illegal dissident groups. President Fidel Castro's government calls the groups "grupusculos," tiny bodies with no significance, and say they are puppets of a U.S. policy seeking to destroy Cuba.
